The <b>Underworks</b> is an [[Areas (Silksong)|area]] in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i>. It is one of the first areas available to explore in [[Act 2]], connected to [[the Citadel]] via the [[Choral Chambers]] and [[Whiteward]]. 

== Description ==
[[File:Screenshot SS Underworks 17.png|thumb|200px|left|Materials falling onto cogs]]
The Underworks is where most of the Citadel's machinery is maintained. The area is dreary, coated in smog from the machinery; its workers endlessly slave away cleaning and maintaining the place in close proximity to deadly hazards like exposed gears or lava pits, with hopes of one day rising to join those in the Citadel itself.<ref>Loam: "Hrrrrrrr. The harder me work, the sooner it come. Thems above, them watch us, always. Work hard, work hard, and us will go up. Hrrrr."</ref> The local amenities are designed to exploit its workers, as benches must be paid for upon each use, and a confessional exists that plays pre-recorded messages that sentence its faithful workers to more work as penance.<ref>Confessional: "Speak now. Thy confession will be heard. ... You have confessed a sin most grave and must by works cleanse yourself. Return to your task and work off-cycle, neither eating nor supping until new-cycle begins." Note that Hornet does not say a word to prompt this response.</ref>
{{Clear}}
== History ==
The Underworks are essential to the function of the Citadel, being where most of the Citadel's machinery is maintained and handling much of its industrial production. The Underworkers were tasked with cleaning and repairing the area, and were promised that if they labored enough they would be welcomed into the Citadel. The Citadel does not appear to have kept this promise.

It is likely that much of the raw materials the Citadel orders the bugs of [[Deep Docks]] to extract are used to supply the Underworks.<ref>[[Flintstone]] Materium description: <i>"Long burning rock from the base of Pharloom. Mined and used by the Citadel in its forgings."</i></ref> 

The Cauldron was likely built after the Weavers left Pharloom, as a damaged Weaver Burial Spire and a re-located [[Spool Fragment]] base can be found in the area. <ref> [[:File:Screenshot_SS_Underworks_15.png| Screenshot of the Clawline Burial Spire.]]</ref>
The Underworks is the home base of the [[Architects]]. The [[Twelfth Architect]] can be found in the eastern section of the area alongside many of their deceased kin.

== How to Access ==
The Underworks is segregated into a west and east half, each part accessible from different points in Act 2.

The western Underworks is commonly accessed from the [[Grand Gate]] after defeating the [[Last Judge]]. Hornet accesses a run-down lift that crashes directly into the Underworks and must find a way to escape into the [[Choral Chambers]] above. Hornet can also access the western Underworks directly through the top of the [[Wisp Thicket]], skipping the Grand Gate. The eastern side is physically obstructed until Hornet unlocks a temporary bridge from that side.

The eastern Underworks houses The Cauldron, and is accessed either from a hidden passage in [[Whiteward]] or from a lift that unlocks after [[Trobbio]]'s defeat. The Cauldron is where Hornet acquires the [[Clawline]] ability, which then must be used to go further east in the Underworks and access the deepest parts of the [[Whispering Vaults]].

<b>The Cauldron</b> is a sub-area located on the right side of the Underworks. It is home to the [[Twelfth Architect]]. It is not initially accessible from the [[Choral Chambers]] entrance to the Underworks, but can be accessed from [[Whiteward]] or the [[Whispering Vaults]]. 

The [[Clawline]] ability is found in this area.

The <b>Chapel of the Architect</b> is a small room to the north of the [[Twelfth Architect]], unlocked using the [[Architect's Key]]. Inside, Hornet may bind the [[Architect Crest]], and find a breakable wall in the top right corner with a [[Needolin Locations#Underworks|Needolin location]] that contains the remains of the 11 other Architects. After binding the Architect Crest and leaving the sub-area, the door closes permanently.

== Trivia ==
* Underworks was originally named Understore, as seen in Ari Gibson's sketchbook.<ref>[[:File:Ari SS Sketch 34.png|Ari Gibson sketch]]</ref>
* While it has direct connections to several parts of the the [[Citadel]], the Underworks is not considered a part of the Citadel proper, as denoted by the [[:File:SS_NavMap.png|zoomed-out map]].
* The confessional is located next to the room with a row of paid-to-use benches in the upper Underworks. It asks for {{R|25}} per use, and gives the same few lines of dialogue every time. Hornet can get to the confessional's other side via a passage at the top of the room, revealing a cogwork statue that gives the dialogue. The statue can be broken, after which the dialogue becomes distorted, but it still requires {{R|25}} nonetheless. (see its dialogue [[Lore Tablets (Silksong)#Underworks|here]])
* The large background fan in the [[Enemy Gauntlets (Silksong)/Underworks 1|enemy gauntlet]] arena causes Hornet's cloak to flutter, in the same way as in windy areas.
* The statues of pilgrims that appear throughout Underworks have golden masks bolted onto them, marked with seal of the Citadel.
